traceability.hint: Every link is verified: the legacy line exists, the target method exists and a passing test names the rule.
traceability.testNotRun: Test named but not run yet

traceability.truncated: Excerpt cut: the file is longer.

stateHint.verified: Every golden or fresh case that exercises this rule matched on both sides in the latest verification.
stateHint.notVerified: The latest verification found no matching case for this rule, or a case that differs.
stateHint.pending: No verification has looked at this rule yet.

traceability.loadError: The traceability could not be loaded
traceability.emptyHint: The comparison appears when the pipeline has extracted rules and generated the code that implements them.

traceability.ruleHint: Computed from the latest verification and its proof pack.

traceability.noTarget: No generated file implements this rule yet.
traceability.behaviourHint: Golden master and fresh inputs that exercise this rule, compared field by field.

limits.samples: Behavior on inputs nobody tried: cases and fresh inputs are samples.
limits.masks: Differences inside fields the comparison ignored (masks and tolerances).

limits.signoff: It does not replace the sign-off of the people who own the system.

validation.signoffHint: PROVEN is evidence, not approval. A named person signs.

validation.loadError: The verdicts could not be loaded

validation.checkNotRun: Not run in this verification: it counts as not checked.
validation.noProofPack: This verdict has no proof pack.
validation.proofPackHint: A zip with the verdict, every case and its differences, the rule trace and the test report, to keep and recompute.

wizard.title: New project
wizard.description: The platform proposes the agents, skills and models from the source, target and architecture. You can change any of them.
wizard.basicsHint: Name the project, choose the flow and the language of the generated artifacts.

flowHint.modernization: Extract the rules from legacy code and rebuild it on a modern stack, with proof of equivalence.
flowHint.newFeature: Build a new feature from user stories, documents, Figma files or screenshots.
flowHint.independentValidation: Validate a migration made by a third party: the platform characterizes the legacy and checks their target against it, with a verdict computed by code.
flowHint.extendExisting: Add a feature to a Spring Boot application that already works: the platform inventories it, generates only the delta from user stories or documents, and proves nothing that worked before breaks.

wizard.artifactLanguageHint: Language of the specification, documentation and reports. Code identifiers are always in English.

compat.mongoModeling: MongoDB needs an extra aggregate modeling step: what is embedded and what is referenced.
compat.serverlessBatch: Long-running COBOL batch does not fit serverless functions; it will use batch or workflow services.
compat.serverlessCics: CICS pseudo-conversational transactions fit stateless serverless services well.
compat.nextBff: Next.js as backend acts as a BFF; domain services are still generated separately.
compat.goConventions: Go uses its own idiomatic pack, not a translation of the Java pack.
compat.upliftOption: .NET Framework to .NET 10 can be an uplift (same structure) or a rewrite. Choose before generation.

usage.title: Usage & costs
usage.description: Tokens and spend of the customer by project, model, phase, agent and provider.
usage.budgetsHint: Alerts at the threshold and at 100 %, once per period. With a hard stop, calls are rejected at 100 % and runs pause at their checkpoint.

usage.failedHint: Errors, policy blocks and budget stops.
usage.costHidden: You can see token usage; amounts in money need the "View costs" permission.
usage.noUsageHint: Model calls appear here as soon as they are made (profile tests included).
usage.alertAtHint: A second alert is always sent at 100 %.
usage.hardStopHint: Without a hard stop the budget only alerts; calls continue past 100 %.

ai.title: AI configuration
ai.description: OpenRouter connections, model catalog, profiles with effort, assignment by phase and agent, pricing and policies.
ai.credentialsNote: The API key is written to the secrets store and never shown again. Every model call goes through the platform's gateway.
ai.catalogHint: Family → exact model version → offering (upstream provider with its own price). Versions are always pinned.
ai.profileHint: An offering plus its parameters. Effort is normalized and translated to each provider's parameter.
ai.fallbackHint: Used when the primary offering is unavailable.
ai.cascade: Configuration cascades: Customer → Project → Phase → Agent role. The most specific assignment wins; an empty level inherits.
ai.pricingHint: Versioned by offering and date. A price change never rewrites past costs.
ai.noTraining: Require providers that do not train on our data
ai.promptsHint: Versioned. Every run records the exact version it used.
ai.evaluationsHint: Measured against a hand-written reference spec: recall, hallucinations and precision errors.
ai.catalogEmptyHint: Sync the catalog with OpenRouter, then load the providers of the models you want to use.
ai.catalogTruncated: Showing {{shown}} of {{total}} models. Refine the search to see the rest.
ai.noConnectionsHint: Add an OpenRouter connection with its API key to start using models.
ai.confirmDeleteConnection: Delete the connection "{{name}}"? Its API key is removed from the secrets store.
ai.noProfiles: No profiles yet. Create one to assign models to phases and agents.
ai.needOfferings: Load the providers of at least one model in the catalog first.
ai.noEffortParameter: no parameter (the model does not support effort)
ai.testProfileHint: The test makes a minimal real call through the gateway; it is recorded in the usage ledger and counts toward budgets.
ai.testOk: It works: {{input}} input and {{output}} output tokens, {{cost}}.
ai.confirmDeleteProfile: Delete the profile "{{name}}"? Its assignments are removed and profiles that fall back to it lose their fallback.
ai.byPhaseHint: Overrides the default for every agent of the phase.
ai.byRoleHint: Overrides the default for the agent in every phase.
ai.combinationsHint: The most specific level: one agent in one phase.
ai.resolveHint: The same cascade the gateway applies on every call.
ai.effortHint: Normalized effort → the real parameter sent to the model. Only the superadministrator edits it.
ai.invalidJson: each value must be a JSON object
ai.allowedProvidersHint: Where the customer's code and data may be sent.
ai.allowedUpstreamHint: Comma-separated tags (anthropic, openai, azure…). Empty allows all.
ai.deniedUpstreamHint: Comma-separated tags; they are never used.

local.title: Models of {{name}}
local.hint: Add the models this server serves, by their exact id. They are visible only to this tenant.
local.noServed: The server lists no models: type the id by hand.
local.serverUnavailable: The server did not list its models; type the id by hand.
local.slugHint: Exactly as the server names it; fixed versions only, no "latest".
local.zdr: The server retains no data (zero data retention)
local.priceHint: USD per million tokens, zero by default. The usage ledger records the tokens and this cost for every call.

adminForms.tenantHint: Creates the customer, its Keycloak organization and its first administrator.

deploymentHint.sharedSaas: Runs on the NexTI shared platform, isolated by customer.
deploymentHint.dedicatedSaas: A dedicated instance operated by NexTI.
deploymentHint.customerCloud: The data plane runs in the customer's cloud account.
deploymentHint.onPrem: Runs in the customer's data center, without internet access.

adminForms.firstAdminHint: Receives an invitation to activate the account and configure MFA.
adminForms.tenantProvisioning: The customer gets its own encryption key, storage prefix and graph database.
adminForms.tenantCreated: Customer "{{name}}" created. Invitation sent to the administrator.
adminForms.inviteHint: Invited people receive an email to activate their account.
adminForms.tenantRolesHint: Optional. Most people only need project roles.
adminForms.inviteFlow: If the email domain uses SSO, the person signs in with their identity provider; otherwise they set a password and MFA.
adminForms.matrixSaved: Permission matrix saved as a new version.
adminForms.idpHint: Connect the customer's identity provider. Keycloak brokers the sign-in.
adminForms.redirectUri: Redirect URI to register in the provider
adminForms.domainsHint: Users with these email domains are routed to this provider.
adminForms.enforceSso: SSO only for these domains (disable password sign-in)
adminForms.keycloakNote: Saved through the Keycloak Admin API. The Keycloak console is never exposed to customers.
adminForms.tenantSlugHint: Lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens. It identifies the customer and cannot be changed later.

inputForms.hint: Every input is validated and scanned before any agent reads it.
inputForms.drop: Drop files here or click to choose
inputForms.acceptedCode: Zip archives or source files. Up to 2 GB.
inputForms.acceptedDocs: PDF, Word, Excel, images. Up to 200 MB each.
inputForms.credentialsHint: Uses a configured integration; no credentials are typed here.
inputForms.pathsHint: Optional. Leave empty for the whole repository.
inputForms.figmaHint: Read through the Figma API: frames, components, variables and prototype navigation.
inputForms.jqlHint: Stories matching this query are synced and kept up to date.

steps.archiveSafety: Zip bombs, path traversal and links

inputForms.finished: All checks passed. The input is ready for the agents.
inputForms.dropScreens: Drop screenshots or click to choose
inputForms.screensHint: PNG or JPG of current or target screens. They are read with vision and turned into screen specifications.
inputForms.prototypeHint: Clickable prototype (Figma prototype, InVision, any https URL). Navigation between screens is read when available.
inputForms.prototypeNotesPlaceholder: What to take from this prototype and what to ignore

decisions.customHint: Be specific: values, conditions and exceptions. It becomes part of the specification.
decisions.commentPlaceholder: Context for the team or the auditor
decisions.recorded: Answer recorded. Agents resume the affected items: {{items}}.
decisions.bulkHint: High-impact questions always need an individual answer.
decisions.empty: Nothing here. Agents keep working and will ask when they need you.

guided.name: Guided
guided.body: A person approves every gate and every P0 rule. Best for the first project with a customer.

balanced.name: Balanced
balanced.body: Gates C1–C4, questions and review by exception. Recommended.

autonomous.name: Autonomous
autonomous.body: Only gates C1 and C4 plus escalated questions. For mature, low-risk work.

when.questions: Questions: when an agent has low confidence, finds a contradiction or two judges disagree. The platform always proposes an answer.
when.reviewAllP0: Review: every P0 rule and every item with low confidence.
when.reviewException: Review by exception: P0 rules, low confidence and a {{pct}}% random sample of the rest.
when.escalations: Escalations: after {{max}} failed self-corrections, with the diagnosis.

hitl.samplingHint: Share of auto-approved items a person still reviews.
hitl.keepsWorking: While a question waits, agents keep working on everything that does not depend on it.

graph.orphansHint: Candidates for dead code or unused data
graph.help: Scroll to zoom · drag to pan · click a node · double-click to zoom in · Esc to reset
graph.emptyPanel: Pick a business flow to see it step by step on the graph, pick a rule to see where it lives, or click any node.

kindHint.orphan: Nothing calls or uses this element. It may be dead code: confirm before migrating it.
kindHint.isolated: This element has no relations at all. It may be unused data or a missing reference in the inventory.

graph.writtenBy: Written by the legacy analyst agent from a source excerpt and the node's connections.
graph.noDescription: No description yet: it is written during the inventory phase.
graph.orderHint: Data and shared layouts first, then programs with the fewest dependents, entry points last. Orphans are left out until confirmed.
graph.loadError: The graph could not be loaded
graph.unavailable: The knowledge graph is not configured in this environment
graph.flowSummary: {{steps}} steps in the order of the code; {{rules}} rules cited along the way.

protoChat.title: Ask for prototype changes
protoChat.subtitle: Chat with the UX/UI designer agent · {{screen}}
protoChat.placeholder: Describe the change, e.g. "make the balance read-only"
protoChat.working: The UX/UI designer is updating the prototype…
protoChat.reply: Done: "{{request}}". The prototype was regenerated as v{{version}} with the approved design system. Review it and approve C2 when ready.
protoChat.empty: Ask for a change and the UX/UI designer will produce a new version.
protoChat.failed: The change could not be sent.
protoChat.readOnly: Your role can see the chat but not ask for changes.

setup.uiHint: Screenshots, Figma files and clickable prototypes. Without them, the platform proposes a design system and prototypes.
setup.invalidLink: Enter a valid https link (for Figma: figma.com/design, /file or /proto).
setup.noUiRefs: No UI references yet. You can add them now or later from the UI design tab.
setup.trackingHint: Link a Jira or Azure DevOps project. The connection is configured once per customer in Administration → Integrations.
setup.integrationHint: Only integrations already connected for this customer appear here.
setup.autoCreate: Create features, stories and tasks automatically when the spec is approved (C1)
setup.dropArchive: Choose the zip or the files with the legacy code
setup.dropExistingArchive: Choose the zip or the files with the application's code
setup.archiveHint: Validated (paths, links, size, malware, secrets) before anything reads it.
setup.gitUrlHint: The platform checks it can read the branch; the clone happens in the preflight.
setup.gitUrlInvalid: Enter an https URL, without credentials.
setup.gitTokenHint: Stored in the secrets store; never shown again.
setup.trackingLater: Linking Jira or Azure DevOps arrives in a later milestone.

backlog.openBugsHint: Found by tester or validator agents
backlog.connectionHint: The project's Jira or Azure DevOps project. The agents create and update its items; the credential is the tenant's.
backlog.automationHint: What agents do in the tracker without being asked.

createFromSpec.name: Create the backlog from the approved spec
createFromSpec.hint: At C1: a feature per feature, the approved stories with their Gherkin and a task per linked element, by wave.

markDone.name: Mark items as done with evidence
markDone.hint: When the verification of their rules passes; the verdict goes as a comment.

bugOnFailure.name: Open a bug when a check fails
bugOnFailure.hint: Steps, expected and obtained, the rules and the trace, from the verdict.

autoFix.name: Start the developer agent on new bugs
autoFix.hint: It proposes a correction in the sandbox; a person reviews it.

backlog.limitsNote: The developer agent stops after the project's maximum of iterations; then the bug is escalated to a person. Closing a bug in the tool does not change a verdict.
backlog.adoProjectHint: The project name in the organization.
backlog.noConnections: The tenant has no Jira or Azure DevOps connection yet: an administrator adds it in Administration → Integrations.
backlog.askOwner: The project owner links the backlog.
backlog.confirmUnlink: Unlink the backlog? The items already created stay in the tool.
backlog.failed: The backlog could not be saved: {{message}}
backlog.syncHint: It runs after C1, after each verdict and when you ask for it.
backlog.syncQueued: Sync queued: the items appear in a moment.
backlog.syncWaiting: A sync is already waiting: it will include the latest changes.
backlog.noItemsHint: They are created when C1 is approved (or with Sync now).
backlog.fixesHint: Corrections the developer agent proposed in the sandbox: drafts a person reviews.

stories.approvedToast: Stories and migration plan approved at C1. The backlog is created in Jira / Azure DevOps.
stories.afterC1: Approved at C1. Any change now is a scope change: only the affected stories go back to review, the impact is recalculated on the graph and the change is synced to Jira / Azure DevOps.
stories.blockers: Before approving C1: {{questions}} with open questions, {{criteria}} without acceptance criteria, {{invalid}} with invalid Gherkin, {{plan}} hard dependency problems in the plan.
stories.readyToApprove: These are the stories that will be built. Review, edit or add stories and approve them with the migration plan at C1 before the migration starts.
stories.coverageHint: Every rule, screen and contract must be in at least one story.
stories.discardedOos: Out of scope: {{reason}}. Its rules are migrated as-is without a story.
stories.noCriteria: No acceptance criteria yet. A story cannot be approved without them.
stories.untracedHint: This story is not linked to any rule, screen, contract or legacy component. Link it or it stays flagged as without traceability.
stories.readOnly: Your role can only view stories.
stories.suggestionsHint: The agent suggests; nothing is applied until a person accepts it.
stories.historyAccepted: Accepted a suggestion from the functional analyst
stories.formHint: Changes create a new version and are recorded in the audit log.
stories.title: Title
stories.criteriaHint: One Gherkin scenario per block, separated by a blank line: Scenario, then Given, When and Then (And/But continue a step). English or Spanish keywords.
stories.dependsOnHint: Hard: cannot be built before it. Soft: can go earlier with a temporary ACL or stub.
stories.auditNote: Who, when and what changed is recorded. After C1 the change becomes a scope change.
stories.splitHint: Choose what moves to the new story. Links to rules and screens are kept.
stories.moveCriteria: Criteria that move to the new story
stories.moveRules: Rules that move to the new story
stories.splitNote: Both stories go back to review. The new story joins the same wave.
stories.mergeHint: Criteria, links and dependencies are joined in this story.
stories.mergeNote: The merged story is kept as "merged" for traceability, and stories that depended on it now depend on this one.
stories.discardHint: A reason is required and is kept in the audit log.
stories.markOutOfScope: Out of scope: its rules are migrated as-is without a story
stories.discardRules: These rules would have no story: {{rules}}.
stories.narrativePlaceholder: As a …, I want …, so that …
stories.noStoriesHint: The pipeline derives them from the rules; you can also create one.
stories.nothingToMerge: There is no other active story to merge.

storyPlan.rejected: Move of {{id}} rejected: it would come before a hard dependency
storyPlan.movedWithWarning: {{id}} moved. It comes before a soft dependency: plan a temporary ACL or stub.
storyPlan.changeAfterC1: Plan changed after C1: recorded as a scope change
storyPlan.hint: Suggested by the platform from the knowledge graph (dependencies, then priority and size). Drag stories between waves or use the arrows; every change is checked against the dependencies.
storyPlan.resetDone: Plan reset to the suggested order
storyPlan.readOnly: Your role can only view the plan. The product owner and the tech lead can change it.
storyPlan.softIssue: Comes before {{dependency}}: needs a temporary ACL or stub.
storyPlan.newWaveHint: Drop a story here to create a wave.
storyPlan.issuesHint: Deterministic check against the graph: hard problems block C1.
storyPlan.noIssues: Every story comes after what it depends on.
storyPlan.diffHint: Stories you moved from the suggested wave.
storyPlan.sameAsSuggested: The plan is the suggested one.
storyPlan.noPlanHint: The pipeline suggests it when it derives the user stories.

problem.cycle: There is a cycle of hard dependencies starting at {{story}}.
problem.unknownStory: {{story}} is not a story of the project.

issue.emptyName: Line {{line}}: the scenario needs a name.
issue.missingGiven: Missing a Given step (the starting situation).
issue.missingThen: Missing a Then step (the expected result).
issue.outOfOrder: Line {{line}}: a {{detail}} step after a {{after}} step. One scenario tests one behavior: split it into two scenarios.
issue.continuationFirst: Line {{line}}: And/But cannot be the first step.
issue.emptyStep: Line {{line}}: the step has no text.
issue.unknownLine: Line {{line}}: "{{detail}}" is not a Gherkin step (Given, When, Then, And, But).
issue.outlineWithoutExamples: A Scenario Outline needs an Examples table.
issue.examplesWithoutOutline: Line {{line}}: Examples only go with a Scenario Outline.
issue.unknownPlaceholder: Line {{line}}: <{{detail}}> is not a column of the Examples table.
issue.emptyExamples: Line {{line}}: the Examples table has no rows.

gherkin.unavailable: The Gherkin check is not available right now; the server validates it again when saving.

api.missingHeader: The scenario must start with "Scenario:" or "Scenario Outline:" (or "Escenario:").
api.missingName: The scenario needs a name after the keyword.
api.missingGiven: Missing a Given step (the starting situation).
api.missingThen: Missing a Then step (the expected result).
api.continuationFirst: And/But can only continue a previous step.
api.outOfOrder: Steps must go Given, then When, then Then.
api.twoBehaviours: A Given or When after a Then describes a second behavior: split the scenario.
api.emptyStep: The step has a keyword and no text.
api.freeText: Every line must be a step, a table row, a doc string, a comment or a tag.
api.missingExamples: A Scenario Outline needs an Examples table.
api.emptyExamples: The Examples table needs a header and at least one row.
api.unknownPlaceholder: A <placeholder> is not a column of the Examples table.
api.duplicateName: Two scenarios of the story have the same name.

runsPage.started: Run launched. The worker picks it up in a moment.
runsPage.oneAtATime: One run at a time per project.
runsPage.emptyHint: Launch the pipeline: the preflight checks inputs, credentials, models and budget before any agent works.

waiting.gate: Waiting for the approval of a gate after {{phase}}.
waiting.question: Waiting for answers to the agents' questions in {{phase}}.
waiting.escalation: An agent could not pass verification in {{phase}}: a person decides how to continue.
waiting.phaseUnavailable: {{phase}} is available from M4: the run waits there, it never skips a phase.

gate.title: Gate {{gate}}
gate.segregation: You launched this run: someone else must decide its gates (segregation of duties).
gate.noPermission: You do not have the permission to decide this gate.
gate.ivvHint: Interface mapping between the legacy and the target
gate.ivvReady: The mapping has no problems: it is ready for C2.
gate.ivvProblems_one: The mapping has {{count}} problem. Correct it in the IV&V tab before approving.
gate.ivvProblems_other: The mapping has {{count}} problems. Correct them in the IV&V tab before approving.
gate.ivvNoMapping: There is no mapping yet: the target has not been taken in.
gate.ivvUnknown: The state of the mapping could not be loaded. Review it in the IV&V tab before approving.

questions.recorded: Answer recorded. The run resumes when no other question is open.

projectCosts.loading: Loading the usage of the project…
projectCosts.loadError: The usage of the project could not be loaded
projectCosts.emptyHint: Nothing consumed yet. Run the pipeline to see where the budget goes, by phase, agent and model.
projectCosts.noUsageView: Seeing usage needs the usage.view permission
projectCosts.noUsageViewHint: Ask a project or tenant administrator for a role that includes it.
projectCosts.tokensOnly: You see tokens only: money needs the cost.view permission.
projectCosts.noBudget: No budget set for this project

integrations.formHint: The token is sent once to the secrets store and is never shown again. Projects of this customer use it to read their Figma files.
integrations.name: Name
integrations.rotateHint: Leave it empty to keep the current token.
integrations.failed: The integration could not be saved: {{message}}
integrations.noneHint: Connect Figma for New Feature projects, and Jira or Azure DevOps for the backlog.
integrations.confirmDelete: Delete the integration {{name}}? Its token is removed from the secrets store.
integrations.note: Tokens live only in the secrets store (OpenBao); the database keeps their path. Every change is audited.

tokenHints.figma: A Figma personal access token with read access to the files.
tokenHints.jira: A Jira API token of the account (basic authentication with its e-mail).
tokenHints.azure_devops: A personal access token with Work Items read and write.

delivery.hardeningHint: Secrets, vulnerable dependencies, insecure patterns and slow tests of the generated code.
delivery.noHardening: The pipeline writes it after the verification (C4).
delivery.releasesHint: Each delivery: pushed to a new branch of your repository, or ready as a ZIP.
delivery.noReleasesHint: The delivery phase of the pipeline, or a push from this tab, creates one.

ivv.loadError: The independent validation could not be loaded
ivv.notYet: The third party target, its mapping and the report appear after the target intake phase.
ivv.inventoryHint: What the worker read of the third party target: its endpoints and its tables.
ivv.noEndpoints: No endpoints were found in the target.
ivv.noTables: No tables were found in the target.
ivv.mappingHint: How each legacy program, field and table maps to the target. It is approved at gate C2.
ivv.mappingUpdated: Last saved {{date}}. It is approved at gate C2.
ivv.readyForC2: The server found no problems in the mapping: it is ready for gate C2.
ivv.problemsTitle_one: {{count}} problem must be corrected before approving C2
ivv.problemsTitle_other: {{count}} problems must be corrected before approving C2
ivv.gapsTitle_one: {{count}} gap found at the target intake
ivv.gapsTitle_other: {{count}} gaps found at the target intake
ivv.gapsHint: What the proposed mapping could not match by name. Fill it in the mapping.
ivv.saveHint: Saving with problems is allowed; the validation fails while any remains.
ivv.savedReady: Mapping saved. It has no problems.
ivv.noPermission: Only someone who can approve gate C2 can change the mapping.
ivv.comparisonHint: The approved legacy rules compared with the rules found in the target. Evidence for the report: the execution decides the verdict.
ivv.reportHint: The report of the independent validation, written by code from the verdict.

delta.loadError: The delta could not be loaded
delta.notYet: The AS-IS inventory, the baseline, the delta design and its files appear as the pipeline produces them.
delta.inventoryHint: What the worker read of the existing application: its endpoints and its tables.
delta.noEndpoints: No endpoints were found in the application.
delta.noTables: No tables were found in the application.
delta.baselineHint: The application's tests run before the delta. Every one that passes here must still pass after it.
delta.noTests: No test passed before the delta: the regression check stays not checked and the verdict cannot be PROVEN.
delta.alreadyFailing_one: {{count}} test already failing before the delta
delta.alreadyFailing_other: {{count}} tests already failing before the delta
delta.alreadyFailingHint: They do not count as a regression.
delta.designHint: The changes the architect proposed from the approved stories and the AS-IS inventory. It is approved at gate C3.
delta.deltaFilesHint: Only the delta is kept: no existing file is deleted. Each file opens in the Code tab.
delta.reportHint: The new and changed files, the stories and the verdict, written by code.
